summary: Elan School, a for-profit troubled-teen facility founded by Joe Ricci in Maine in the early 1970s, controlled minors through peer surveillance, public humiliation and beatings in a boxing ring until it closed in 2011.

evidence.note: Ricci's birth in Port Chester, NY in 1945 and childhood get a long segment
In 1971 the couple decide to open their own therapeutic community
School finally closes in 2011 after survivor campaign
Davidson as absentee psychiatrist partner lending credibility and referring patients
Founders move to Maine for its lax licensing rules; first site in Naples
Main campus at Poland Spring, Maine, plus Parsonsfield facility
1974 fire at Sebago site and inflated insurance claim; pattern of insurance fraud
Ricci's own opiate addiction, enabled by Davidson's prescriptions
Synanon as a drug-rehab cult that seeded the troubled teen industry
Court-referred teens face prison if they leave; police return or release runaways
Account of teenager Phil Newell collapsing and dying after the ring
Ricci uses Elan humiliation tactics on his wife Sherry; she is hospitalized in 1976

notes: Title names the school, so Elan is the sole primary and roles are empty; Ricci arguably co-primary. Packet spells him Richie; Ricci per footnotes. Founding 1971 per transcript (some sources 1970). Phil Newell death year garbled in transcript. cults-new-religions rests on Synanon segment and cult framing; policing-incarceration on court referrals and runaway policing (weaker). Smith rape victim was 16, so no sexual-violence warning.
